domain: A genuine sibling of the template's Menu_MoveSelectionForward: it operates on the exact same menu-state struct (the byte offsets 0x394/0x39c/0x39e/0x3a2/0x348 that the template names count/selection/index/status/list all recur here at the identical addresses, confirmed by cross-reading both raw disassemblies), calling the same Func_0801b9a8/Func_0801b9ec/Func_0801ba68/Func_080030f8/Func_0801b010 helpers, but adds a substantially larger body: after advancing the selection index it inspects a table slot (state+916) and, when a specific end-of-list condition is hit, walks a singly linked list rooted at state+0x348 (next pointer at node offset 4) twice -- once to stamp interior nodes with 'count'/'selection'-derived visual fields and a distinct value on the last node, once (after a Func_0801bd98 callback per node) to restripe every node's position fields by a fixed 16-unit step.
behavior: reads a table-slot halfword at state+916; if it is <=5, only handles a narrower 'slot==*count' case (clearing state+924) and falls through to the shared tail

if the slot is >5 and (selection-table value + index) equals it, walks the state+0x348 linked list: stamps every interior node's base/status/y-ish fields from *count/*selection, stamps the terminal node with status=16, then busy-waits (WaitFrames loop) until a node field settles; then calls Func_0801bd98 once per node with per-index halfword pairs from around state+852; then zeroes count/selection and re-walks the list a second time restriping node fields with a running value that starts from the terminal node's field and steps by 16 per node, tagging each with status=12
in the >5-but-not-matching case, mirrors the template's own 'index==4' branch structure (decrement index, set two byte-ish flags, advance selection, call Func_0801ba68, possible extra clear)
shared tail: status=1; Func_0801b9ec(state, index); WaitFrames(1); Func_0801b010 using the halfword at list_head+10; WaitFrames(1)

bounded_search.reason: One complete-behavior candidate was written and scored. It is 64 bytes over reference (492 vs 428) and needs 4 extra callee-saved registers (fp, sl, r8, r9 all pushed) versus reference's 2 (sl, r8), showing the source shape carries far more simultaneously-live locals than the real function used -- a genuinely different, more time-intensive respelling pass (collapsing the temporaries introduced for readability back into the same handful of registers reference reuses across the linked-list walks) would be needed before iterating on exactness.

remaining: This owner (and its sibling 0801b810) turned out to be substantially larger and more involved than the family's other 'small, under ~600 byte' members -- a full byte-exact reconstruction needs a dedicated pass, not the bounded per-owner budget used for the rest of this batch. The behavioral read above is solid (struct offsets are corroborated against the already-adopted template, not guessed) and is a reasonable starting point for that future pass. The likely next step is reducing live-range overlap in the two list-walk blocks so the compiler doesn't need more than two callee-saved scratch registers, matching reference's r8/sl usage.
